en: Haddab ibn Khalid al-Azdi narrated to us, Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, Humayd ibn Hilal informed us, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Samit, who said: Abu Dharr said: We departed from our people Ghifar—and they used to make the sacred month lawful. So I departed, along with my brother Unays and our mother, and we stayed with a maternal uncle of ours. Our maternal uncle honored us and treated us well. But his people envied us and said: "Whenever you leave your family, Unays goes behind your back to them." So our maternal uncle came and relayed to us what had been said to him. I said to him: "As for your past kindness, you have ruined it, and there can be no union between us hereafter." So we brought our herd of livestock close, loaded onto them, and our maternal uncle covered himself with his garment and began to weep. We departed until we settled in the vicinity of Mecca. Unays then competed in a contest of poetic boasting for our herd and an equal amount to match it. They both went to the soothsayer, who judged in favor of Unays. So Unays came to us with our herd and an equal herd along with it. He said: And I had already been praying, O son of my brother, three years before meeting the Messenger of Allah (pbuh). I said, "To whom?" He said, "To Allah." I said, "So where did you face?" He said, "I faced wherever my Lord directed me. I would pray late into the evening until, toward the end of the night, I would collapse as if I were a piece of cloth until the sun rose over me." Then Unays said: "I have some business in Mecca, so look after my affairs." Unays departed until he reached Mecca, but he was delayed in returning to me. Then he arrived, and I said: "What did you do?" He said: "I met a man in Mecca upon your religion, who claims that Allah has sent him." I said: "So what do the people say?" He said: "They say: a poet, a soothsayer, a sorcerer." And Unays was one of the poets. Unays said: "I have heard the speech of the soothsayers, and it is not their speech. And I measured his speech against the meters of poetry, and it does not conform to the tongue of anyone after me to say that it is poetry. By Allah, he is truly truthful, and they are liars!" He said: I said, "So look after my affairs until I go and see." He said: So I came to Mecca, and I approached a man among them whom I deemed weak and said: "Where is this one whom you call the Sabaean?" He pointed at me and shouted: "The Sabaean!" Thereupon the people of the valley turned against me with every clod of earth and bone until I fell down unconscious. He said: When I arose, I arose looking like a red sacrificial stone. He said: So I came to Zamzam, washed the blood off myself, and drank of its water. And indeed, O son of my brother, I stayed for thirty, between night and day, having no food except Zamzam water. I grew so fat that the folds of my belly creased, and I felt no weakness of hunger in my liver. He said: While the people of Mecca were in a bright, moonlit night, when a slumber fell upon their ears, so that no one was circumambulating the House except two women from among them who were calling upon Isaf and Na'ilah. He said: They passed by me in their circumambulation, and I said: "Marry one to the other!" He said: But they did not desist from their words. He said: They passed by me again, and I said: "[An idol with] a private organ like a piece of wood—except that I did not speak euphemistically." So they turned away wailing and saying: "If only there were someone here from our men!" He said: The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) and Abu Bakr met them as the two were descending. He said: "What is the matter with you two?" They said: "The Sabaean between the Ka'bah and its coverings!" He said: "What did he say to you two?" They said: "He spoke to us a foul word that fills the mouth." And the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) came until he touched the Black Stone and circumambulated the House, he and his companion, then he prayed. When he finished his prayer—Abu Dharr said—I was the first person to greet him with the greeting of Islam. He said: I said, "Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "And upon you, and the mercy of Allah." Then he said: "Who are you?" He said: I said, "From Ghifar." He said: He moved his hand and placed his fingers upon his forehead. I said to myself: "He disliked that I affiliated myself with Ghifar." So I went to take his hand, but his companion restrained me—and he knew him better than I did. Then he raised his head and said: "When did you arrive here?" He said: I said, "I have been here for thirty, between night and day." He said: "And who has been feeding you?" He said: I said, "I had no food except Zamzam water, and I have grown fat until the folds of my belly creased, and I do not feel any weakness of hunger in my liver." He said: "Indeed, it is blessed; it is food that nourishes." Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, permit me to host him tonight." So the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) and Abu Bakr set out, and I set out with them. Abu Bakr opened a door and began taking handfuls of raisins of al-Ta'if for us, and that was the first food I ate there. Then I remained for as long as I remained, then I came to the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) and he said: "A land of date palms has been shown to me; I see it to be none other than Yathrib. Will you convey from me to your people? Perhaps Allah will benefit them through you and reward you regarding them." So I came to Unays, and he said: "What did you do?" I said: "I have embraced Islam and believed." He said: "I have no dislike for your religion; indeed, I too have embraced Islam and believed." Then we came to our mother, and she said: "I have no dislike for the religion of you two; indeed, I too have embraced Islam and believed." So we loaded up until we reached our people Ghifar, and half of them embraced Islam. They were led in prayer by Imah ibn Rahadah al-Ghifari, and he was their leader. And half of them said: "When the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) arrives in Medina, we will embrace Islam." So when the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) arrived in Medina, the remaining half embraced Islam. And the tribe of Aslam came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, our brothers; we embrace Islam upon that which they embraced Islam." So they embraced Islam. Thereupon the Messenger of Allah (pbuh) said: "Ghifar—may Allah forgive them; and Aslam—may Allah preserve them in peace."
